abstract: We develop a method for approximate synthesis of single–qubit rotations of the form $e^{-if(\phi_{1},\ldots,\phi_{k})X}$ that is based on the Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) framework for quantum circuit synthesis. We demonstrate how smooth computable functions $f$ can be synthesized from two basic primitives. This synthesis approach constitutes a manifestly quantum form of arithmetic that differs greatly from the approaches commonly used in quantum algorithms. The key advantage of our approach is that it requires far fewer qubits than existing approaches: as a case in point, we show that using as few as $3$ ancilla qubits, one can obtain RUS circuits for approximate multiplication and reciprocals. We also analyze the costs of performing multiplication and inversion on a quantum computer using conventional approaches and find that they can require too many qubits to execute on a small quantum computer, unlike our approach.

specification.problem: Approximately synthesize single-qubit rotations e^{-i f(phi_1,...,phi_k) X}, for smooth computable f, using the Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) framework built from two basic primitives. Examples are approximate multiplication and reciprocals with as few as 3 ancilla qubits. The approach is compared on qubit cost with conventional quantum arithmetic.

specification.initial_state: All qubits in |0>; the input angles phi_j enter as rotation gates, so no separate input register is used (assumed).

steps.description: Prepare the target and ancilla qubits in |0> or |+> (assumed).
Apply the two basic primitives (unspecified in the abstract), interleaved with the input rotations by phi_j, to compose the function f on the target.
Measure the ancillas. On the success outcome the target holds the approximation of R_f. On failure, correct or reset and repeat the attempt.

specification.measurement: Ancilla qubits are measured each RUS attempt; one outcome pattern (unspecified in the abstract) signals success, the others failure (assumed).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical control repeats the attempt on failure, with any correction as needed, until success (assumed generic RUS logic).
assumptions: Multiplication and reciprocal are taken to be f=phi1*phi2 and f=1/phi
